author: Mark Atwood
text: Rust idiom confidence (rusty pass #3): 22% chance of missed issue (DOWN from 25% in pass #2). Confidence improved marginally because (a) every prior idiom finding has now been visited at least once and the fix-side diffs are individually scoped to one finding, making line-by-line audit straightforward; (b) the new patterns introduced (bool_arg helpers, maintain_indexes_after_set, iterator-chain re-index, typed UTCDate parsing) are byte-identical-behavior refactors that don't introduce new design space. Did NOT run cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings against the post-fix tree (review-readonly mode); did NOT run cargo test --workspace; did NOT cross-check MSRV against the is_some_and (1.70) and Option::copied (1.35) calls (workspace MSRV is 1.88 per the .43 commit text, so both are fine). Least confident: (a) whether the marginal duplication of KNOWN_TYPES between MemoryBackend::seed_object and MockBackend::seed_object (4-item string list in two sites) is worth a P3 finding — opted not to file because the absolute size is tiny, both lists are pub(crate)/test-only, and the principled fix (typestate-tagged seed) is the same workspace-foundation work deferred at JMAP-934u and .44; (b) whether the new match-and-Some-wrap pattern in the typed-UTCDate threading (event.rs:78-94) should be flagged as 'could be .map().transpose()?' — opted not to because the match form is more readable and the engineering basis is thin; reasonable Rust practitioners disagree on this. Would raise confidence to 15-18% if I ran cargo clippy --all-features against the post-fix tree to catch anything mechanical I missed. Stopping the review loop on the rusty axis per the workspace bikeshedding-signal rule: three consecutive passes with zero new beads filed, all remaining open idiom findings are either P2-and-deferred-to-canonical-propagation or P3+-and-opinion-labeled.
